title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations
summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 2 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God made the night a garment, sleep a rest, and the day a rising (nushūr) (weight 6.3); God makes winds his messengers (angels) and flaming fire his ministers (weight 5.8); A solid firmament (raqia) separates upper waters from lower waters (weight 5.6); God sends the winds as heralds before his mercy and sends down pure water from the sky (weight 5.4); Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons (weight 4.7); Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection (weight 4.4). Pair score 32.3.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; and 35 more.

Only in The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations: God extends the shadow, makes the sun its guide, then draws it back gently; God created humans from water and gave them kinship by blood and by marriage; Told to prostrate to the Merciful, the pagans ask 'What is al-Raḥmān?'; What God does after creating in six days [divergence between the texts]; Worship of the constellations or zodiac signs (mazzalot); God has inscribed a circle on the face of the waters at the boundary between light and darkness; As a sign the shadow goes back ten steps on the stairway (dial) of Ahaz; God set constellations (buruj) in the sky and adorned it for beholders; God the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting (al-hayy al-qayyum); God let loose the two seas, one sweet, one salt, with a barrier (barzakh) and partition between them; Creation is completed in six days; After creating the heavens and earth God established himself on the Throne (istawa 'ala l-'arsh); and 1 more.

title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ The Originator, winged angels, and the two seas
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/06-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Sun and moon are subjected, each running to an appointed term (weight 5.8); God makes winds his messengers (angels) and flaming fire his ministers (weight 5.8); God sends the winds as heralds before his mercy and sends down pure water from the sky (weight 5.4); Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection (weight 4.4). Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; and 37 more.

title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ Ha-Mim: the signs, the scornful liar, Israel's book and the Prophet's shari'a
summary: 2 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Catalogue of signs: heavens and earth, alternation of night and day, ships, rain reviving dead earth, beasts, winds, clouds (weight 5.6); Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection (weight 4.4). Pair score 10.0.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; and 39 more.

Only in Ha-Mim: the signs, the scornful liar, Israel's book and the Prophet's shari'a: God has subjected (sakhkhara) to humans the sea and all that is in the heavens and on the earth; Believers are to forgive those who do not look for 'the days of God'; God himself will requite; God gave the Children of Israel the Book, judgment (hukm) and prophethood, good provision, and preferred them over the worlds; God set the Prophet upon a clear way (shari'a) of the command, to follow and not the desires of the ignorant; Earlier communities split into factions only after knowledge came to them, out of rivalry (baghy) among themselves; How much of creation is put under man's rule or use [divergence between the texts]; Israel given God's law, as a unique gift or followed by a later law [divergence between the texts]; Woe to every sinful liar who hears God's signs recited, persists in arrogance as if he had not heard, and takes them in mockery; Formula: the sending down of the Book (tanzil al-kitab) is from God, the Mighty, the Wise/Knowing; Vengeance and recompense are mine; Whoever does good does it for his own soul; whoever does evil, it is against it; Humans given rule over animals; and 1 more.

matches.note: Winds as God's agents: ʿōśeh malʾāḵâw rûḥôṯ məšārəṯâw ʾēš lōhēṭ vs. wa-dh-dhāriyāti dharwan fa-l-ḥāmilāti wiqran fa-l-jāriyāti yusran fa-l-muqassimāti amran. The psalm makes winds God's messengers; the Quran swears by winds (or angels) that scatter, carry and distribute the command. title: Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten) ↔ Al-Rahman: the Merciful taught the Quran; sun and moon by reckoning; clay and smokeless fire; the two seas and the barrier
summary: 3 correspondences read side by side: 3 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The sun and the moon run by exact reckoning (husban) (weight 6.7); All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n) (weight 6.7); Man created from ringing clay like pottery, the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire (marij min nar) (weight 6.7); Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons (weight 4.7). Pair score 24.8.

Only in Psalm 104, the great creation hymn (cf. the Great Hymn to the Aten): When God takes away their breath creatures die and return to dust; when he sends his spirit they are created; Hymn praising God as creator, describing the ordering of the cosmos and its creatures; Each creature has its God-given habitat: birds in cedars, stork in junipers, ibex in mountains, hyrax in rocks; God rejoices in his works; Leviathan was formed to sport in the sea, or for God to play with; God sends forth his spirit and renews the face of the earth; At God's rebuke and thunder the primeval waters flee from the mountains to their appointed place; God gives wine to gladden the heart of man, oil to make his face shine and bread to sustain him; Self-exhortation 'Bless YHWH, O my soul'; God makes the clouds his chariot and walks on the wings of the wind; God takes life and gives it again [divergence between the texts]; God looks at the earth and it trembles, touches the mountains and they smoke; and 37 more.

Only in Al-Rahman: the Merciful taught the Quran; sun and moon by reckoning; clay and smokeless fire; the two seas and the barrier: God raised the sky and set the Balance: do not transgress in the balance; weigh with justice and do not skimp; Lord of the two easts and the two wests (the solstitial sunrises and sunsets); The Merciful (al-Rahman) taught the Quran, created man and taught him clear speech (bayan); From the two seas come pearls and coral (marjan); A creation litany with a refrain after every line [divergence between the texts]; The text addresses jinn and humans together in the dual ('you two', al-thaqalan, 'the two weighty ones'); Earth and heavens will perish and wear out like a garment, changed like clothing, but God remains the same; Just weights and measures, and the ground given for them [divergence between the texts]; Refrain repeated 31 times: 'Which then of the bounties of your Lord will you two (jinn and humans) deny?'; Ships running on the sea like landmarks/mountains are a sign; God could still the wind and leave them motionless or wreck them; The star (or herb, najm) and the tree prostrate themselves to God; All on earth perish; there remains the Face of your Lord, possessor of majesty and honor; and 6 more.

title: Psalm 139, God's all-knowing presence and the embryo ↔ Man from clay through the stages of the womb; seven paths, water, Sinai's tree, cattle and ships
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/05-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Humans created from dust, then a drop (nuṭfa), then a clinging clot (ʿalaqa), then a chewed lump (muḍgha), shaped and unshaped (weight 6.3); God's eyes saw the speaker's unformed substance (golem); all his days were written in God's book before one of them existed (weight 6.3); God poured the embryo out like milk and curdled it like cheese, clothing it with skin and flesh and knitting bones and sinews (weight 5.8). Only in Psalm 139, God's all-knowing presence and the embryo: Darkness is not dark to God; night shines like day, darkness and light are alike; 'YHWH, you have searched me and known me': God knows sitting and rising, thoughts from afar, every word before it is spoken; Nowhere to flee God's spirit: if I ascend to heaven you are there, if I make my bed in Sheol you are there; 'Do I not hate those who hate you, YHWH? Only in Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David: God sends a band (mishlahat) of 'evil angels' (mal'akhei ra'im) to execute his wrath; Manna called 'bread of the mighty ones' (lehem abbirim), i.e. food of angels; God struck his enemies backward/in the rear (read by rabbis as the Philistines' hemorrhoids); The exodus wonders are located in 'the field of Zoan' (Tanis); The Lord awakes as from sleep like a warrior shouting from wine; God remembers that humans are flesh, a breath that passes and does not return; God rejected the tent of Joseph and tribe of Ephraim and chose Judah and Mount Zion; In the catastrophe young men are consumed by fire, maidens have no wedding song, widows do not lament; God built his sanctuary like the heights (or heavens) and like the earth founded forever; God took David from the sheepfolds, from following the nursing ewes, to shepherd his people; The ark of God is captured by enemies; God commanded the skies and opened the doors (or windows) of heaven; and 27 more.

Only in Psalm 105, historical hymn from the patriarchs through Joseph and the exodus: Egypt rejoiced when Israel left, for dread of them had fallen on it; God turned the Egyptians' hearts to hate his people and deal craftily with them; Joseph's feet were hurt in fetters and his neck (nefesh) put in iron until his word came true; God sent a man ahead of them: Joseph, sold as a slave; Joseph was to bind the king's princes at will and teach his elders wisdom; At the exodus not one among the tribes stumbled (or was feeble); God calls the patriarchs his 'anointed ones' and 'prophets' and rebukes kings for their sake ('Touch not my anointed'); God opened the rock and waters gushed and ran as a river in the desert; The ancestors were few in number, sojourners wandering from nation to nation; The chain of patriarchs to whom revelation or covenant passed [divergence between the texts]; The number of signs or plagues in Egypt [divergence between the texts]; A palpable darkness covers the land for three days; and 19 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/04-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Moses was given nine clear signs [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); The returning waters drown the pursuing army; not one survives (weight 4.5). Pair score 10.8.

Only in Psalm 78, Asaph's historical recital from Egypt to David: God sends a band (mishlahat) of 'evil angels' (mal'akhei ra'im) to execute his wrath; Manna called 'bread of the mighty ones' (lehem abbirim), i.e. food of angels; God struck his enemies backward/in the rear (read by rabbis as the Philistines' hemorrhoids); The exodus wonders are located in 'the field of Zoan' (Tanis); The Lord awakes as from sleep like a warrior shouting from wine; God remembers that humans are flesh, a breath that passes and does not return; God rejected the tent of Joseph and tribe of Ephraim and chose Judah and Mount Zion; In the catastrophe young men are consumed by fire, maidens have no wedding song, widows do not lament; God built his sanctuary like the heights (or heavens) and like the earth founded forever; God took David from the sheepfolds, from following the nursing ewes, to shepherd his people; The ark of God is captured by enemies; God commanded the skies and opened the doors (or windows) of heaven; and 39 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Protection from the terror of the night, the arrow by day, the pestilence (dever) stalking in darkness and Qeteb that ravages at noon (weight 6.7); Psalm used as protection against demons and harm (later amulet and 'song of plagues') (weight 6.3). Pair score 13.0.

Only in Sincerity, daybreak and mankind: God's unity and the two refuges: Refuge from the evil of darkness (or the moon) when it settles (ghasiq idha waqab); Refuge from the evil of an envier when he envies (evil eye); God is al-Samad (the Eternal Refuge, the solid one who needs nothing); Triple title: Lord of mankind, King of mankind, God of mankind; Refuge from the evil of the slinking whisperer (al-waswas al-khannas) who whispers in people's breasts, from jinn and humans; God does not beget and was not begotten; God does not beget and was not begotten [contrast between the texts]; Protective formula 'Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of...' (qul a'udhu bi-rabbi) against named evils; Refuge from the evil of those (women) who blow on knots (al-naffathat fi al-'uqad), i.e. knot-tying sorcery; Cluster of divine epithets in sequence (e.g. the Forgiving, the Loving, Lord of the Throne, the Glorious, doer of what he wills; or Lord, King, God of mankind); 'To whom will you liken God, what likeness compare to him?'; 'There is none like you and no God beside you'; and 1 more.

title: Psalm 96, sing a new song; the gods of the nations are nothings ↔ Al-Rahman: the Merciful taught the Quran; sun and moon by reckoning; clay and smokeless fire; the two seas and the barrier
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The star (or herb, najm) and the tree prostrate themselves to God (weight 6.7); Hills, meadows, valleys, sea, rivers or trees rejoice, clap or sing before God (weight 5.3). Pair score 12.0.

Only in Psalm 96, sing a new song; the gods of the nations are nothings: Formula 'Ascribe (havu) to YHWH glory and strength', addressed to divine beings or the families of peoples; Bow down to YHWH in the splendor of holiness (hadrat qodesh); All the gods of the peoples are 'elilim' (nonentities), but YHWH made the heavens; God comes to judge the earth with righteousness, and all creation rejoices; Enthronement acclamation 'YHWH reigns (YHWH malakh)', the world firmly established and unshakable; YHWH is great and to be feared above all gods; All the earth or all peoples are summoned to shout and sing to God; Call to sing a new song (shir hadash) to God; A psalm or section duplicates another psalm with variations (often divine-name change).

Only in Al-Rahman: the Merciful taught the Quran; sun and moon by reckoning; clay and smokeless fire; the two seas and the barrier: God raised the sky and set the Balance: do not transgress in the balance; weigh with justice and do not skimp; Lord of the two easts and the two wests (the solstitial sunrises and sunsets); The Merciful (al-Rahman) taught the Quran, created man and taught him clear speech (bayan); From the two seas come pearls and coral (marjan); A creation litany with a refrain after every line [divergence between the texts]; The text addresses jinn and humans together in the dual ('you two', al-thaqalan, 'the two weighty ones'); All in heaven and earth ask of him; every day he is engaged in some affair (kull yawm huwa fi sha'n); Earth and heavens will perish and wear out like a garment, changed like clothing, but God remains the same; Man created from ringing clay like pottery, the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire (marij min nar); Just weights and measures, and the ground given for them [divergence between the texts]; Refrain repeated 31 times: 'Which then of the bounties of your Lord will you two (jinn and humans) deny?'; Ships running on the sea like landmarks/mountains are a sign; God could still the wind and leave them motionless or wreck them; and 8 more.

Only in Eighth vision, four chariots between bronze mountains: Four chariots come out from between two mountains of bronze; The chariots are the four winds (spirits) of heaven that go out after presenting themselves before the Lord of all the earth; The horses going to the north country have set God's spirit at rest there; Horses of different colors (red, sorrel, white, black, dappled) are sent out by God through the earth; A heavenly being reports he has been roaming to and fro on the earth.

Only in Those sent forth: the refrain of woe: Humans created from a despised fluid placed in a secure lodging (the womb) for a known term; On that day the damned do not speak and are not permitted to offer excuses; The earth is made a receptacle (kifat) that holds the living and the dead; Hell throws sparks as huge as castles, like yellow (or black) camels; The damned are led to a shadow of three branches that gives no shade nor protects from the flame; Every verse ends with the same response ('for his steadfast love is forever'), an antiphonal litany; In paradise the shades are close and the fruit clusters hang low within reach; Stars and constellations (kesilim) give no light, the sun is dark at its rising and the moon does not shine; Refrain 'Woe that day to the deniers' (waylun yawma'idhin lil-mukadhdhibin) repeated through a surah; At the end the sky is split, cleft or opened (infatarat, inshaqqat, furijat); At the end the mountains become a heap of running sand, are blown away, set in motion or turn into a mirage; God set the mountains as pegs or firm anchors (awtad, rawasi) for the earth; and 2 more.

title: Zephaniah's Day of YHWH against Judah ↔ Al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat; angelic intercession; the scrolls of Abraham and Moses; the Lord of Sirius
summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: 'The imminent (al-azifa) has drawn near'; none but God can remove it (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Zephaniah's Day of YHWH against Judah: Men thickened on their lees who say in their hearts 'YHWH will do neither good nor evil'; The Day of YHWH is a sacrifice he has prepared, with invited guests consecrated; Litany of the Day: day of wrath, distress, ruin, darkness, cloud and thick darkness, shofar and alarm; God will search Jerusalem with lamps to find the complacent; Named districts of Jerusalem (Fish Gate, Mishneh/Second Quarter, Maktesh/Mortar) wail; A prophet's genealogy is traced several generations back to a king (Hezekiah); God will punish officials and princes who wear foreign garments; People bow and swear both by YHWH and by Malkam (their king or Milcom); God will sweep away humans, beasts, birds of the air and fish of the sea from the face of the ground (creation reversed); Idolatrous priests (kemarim) who burned incense to Baal, sun, moon, constellations are put down; Priests do not tread on a temple threshold, explained by an event; 'Hush (has) before YHWH, all the earth', for he is in his holy temple or has roused himself; and 7 more.

Only in Al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat; angelic intercession; the scrolls of Abraham and Moses; the Lord of Sirius: The three goddesses al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat, 'the third, the other', named and rejected; They follow only conjecture (zann), and conjecture avails nothing against the truth; God created the pairs, male and female, from a drop of sperm (nutfa) when it is emitted; A surah ends with the command to prostrate (sajda verse); God destroyed 'Ad 'the first' (implying a second 'Ad); God knew you when he produced you from the earth and when you were embryos in your mothers' bellies; do not claim purity; The idols are only names you and your fathers have named, for which God sent down no authority; God is 'the Lord of Sirius' (al-shi'ra), a star worshipped by some Arabs; Those who avoid the great sins and indecencies, except minor slips (al-lamam), find God's forgiveness wide; To your Lord is the final end (al-muntaha); 'Is the male for you and the female for him? That is an unfair division'; 'Which of your Lord's bounties (ala') will you dispute/deny?'; and 15 more.

summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The Day of YHWH: a coming day of divine judgment, terror and darkness (weight 5.0). Pair score 5.0.

Only in Zephaniah's Day of YHWH against Judah: Men thickened on their lees who say in their hearts 'YHWH will do neither good nor evil'; The Day of YHWH is a sacrifice he has prepared, with invited guests consecrated; Litany of the Day: day of wrath, distress, ruin, darkness, cloud and thick darkness, shofar and alarm; God will search Jerusalem with lamps to find the complacent; Named districts of Jerusalem (Fish Gate, Mishneh/Second Quarter, Maktesh/Mortar) wail; A prophet's genealogy is traced several generations back to a king (Hezekiah); God will punish officials and princes who wear foreign garments; People bow and swear both by YHWH and by Malkam (their king or Milcom); God will sweep away humans, beasts, birds of the air and fish of the sea from the face of the ground (creation reversed); Idolatrous priests (kemarim) who burned incense to Baal, sun, moon, constellations are put down; 'The imminent (al-azifa) has drawn near'; none but God can remove it; Priests do not tread on a temple threshold, explained by an event; and 7 more.

passages.text: وَٱتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ نُوحٍ إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِۦ يَٰقَوْمِ إِن كَانَ كَبُرَ عَلَيْكُم مَّقَامِى وَتَذْكِيرِى بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ فَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ فَأَجْمِعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَكُمْ وَشُرَكَآءَكُمْ ثُمَّ لَا يَكُنْ أَمْرُكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ غُمَّةً ثُمَّ ٱقْضُوٓا۟ إِلَىَّ وَلَا تُنظِرُونِ
فَإِن تَوَلَّيْتُمْ فَمَا سَأَلْتُكُم مِّنْ أَجْرٍ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِ وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ

sides.note: Noah before the flood: in Gen he says nothing to anyone and simply obeys (wayyaʿaś nōaḥ kᵉkōl ʾăšer ṣiwwāh ʾōtô ʾĕlōhîm kēn ʿāśāh); in Q he preaches and challenges his people: yā qawmi in kāna kabura ʿalaykum maqāmī wa-tadhkīrī bi-āyāti llāhi ... fa-ajmiʿū amrakum wa-shurakāʾakum. Q adds the speech.

passages.text: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنِّى لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ
أَن لَّا تَعْبُدُوٓا۟ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ

فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا نَرَىٰكَ إِلَّا بَشَرًا مِّثْلَنَا وَمَا نَرَىٰكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِىَ ٱلرَّأْىِ وَمَا نَرَىٰ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا مِن فَضْلٍۭ بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كَٰذِبِينَ

sides.note: Noah and his people before the flood: Gen records no word from Noah, only obedience (wayyaʿaś nōaḥ kᵉkōl ʾăšer-ṣiwwāhû YHWH); Q adds a long debate, innī lakum nadhīrun mubīnun an lā taʿbudū illā llāha, with the chiefs' replies (mā narāka illā basharan mithlanā) and their mockery while he builds (sakhirū minhu).

passages.text: فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ فِى ٱلْفُلْكِ وَجَعَلْنَٰهُمْ خَلَٰٓئِفَ وَأَغْرَقْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ

sides.note: Why the generation drowns: in Q because they rejected the messenger (wa-aghraqnā lladhīna kadhdhabū bi-āyātinā); in Gen because the earth was full of violence and corruption (wattimmālēʾ hāʾāreṣ ḥāmās ... kî-hišḥît kol-bāśār ʾet-darkô). Moral corruption becomes rejection of a prophet.

passages.text: فَقَالَ ٱلْمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن قَوْمِهِۦ مَا نَرَىٰكَ إِلَّا بَشَرًا مِّثْلَنَا وَمَا نَرَىٰكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِىَ ٱلرَّأْىِ وَمَا نَرَىٰ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا مِن فَضْلٍۭ بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كَٰذِبِينَ
وَٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

sides.note: Why they drown: Gen, the earth full of violence (kî-mālᵉʾāh hāʾāreṣ ḥāmās mippᵉnêhem); Q, rejecting the messenger and doing wrong (lladhīna ẓalamū innahum mughraqūn), after Noah's preaching. In Gen all flesh perishes (qēṣ kol-bāśār); in Q 'Noah's people'.

title: Lot, his guests, his daughters and the stones of sijjil ↔ Abraham's guests and the destruction of Lot's people (Surah 15:51-77)
summary: 6 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place (weight 6.3); Lot's wife is among those who stay behind and perish (weight 6.3); Stones of baked clay (sijjil), in layers, each marked by the Lord, rain on the town (weight 6.3); Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom (weight 6.0); Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests (weight 6.0); Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed (weight 5.6). Pair score 36.4.

Only in Lot, his guests, his daughters and the stones of sijjil: The angels tell Lot the destruction is appointed for the morning: 'is not the morning near?'; Lot wishes he had strength or a strong support to take refuge in; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; Only Lot's household is brought out of the doomed city; What Lot says to the townsmen; How Lot receives the heavenly guests [divergence between the texts]; When Lot leaves the city and when the destruction falls [divergence between the texts]; Lot's townspeople turn on him; What falls from heaven on Sodom; A land will be overthrown like Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors, never inhabited; The fate of Lot's wife; God casts great hailstones from heaven, killing more than the sword; and 2 more.

Only in Abraham's guests and the destruction of Lot's people (Surah 15:51-77): The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people; The rescued family leaves by night, the leader following behind them; God swears by the prophet's life (la-'amruka); The patriarch tells his unknown guests 'we are afraid of you'; The ruins of the destroyed towns lie on a road still traveled; Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom [divergence between the texts]; The angelic guests reveal they are sent against a criminal people [divergence between the texts]; Cities overturned (hafakh) and the plain destroyed [divergence between the texts]; The doomed people are seized by the Shout (al-sayha) at dawn or sunrise; Do not despair of God's mercy (rawh / rahma); only unbelievers or the astray despair; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place [divergence between the texts]; Host offers his virgin daughters to the mob to protect his guests [divergence between the texts]; and 9 more.

title: Lot, his guests, his daughters and the stones of sijjil ↔ Lot and the destruction of his town
summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Two angels are received as guests by Lot in Sodom (weight 6.0); A land will be overthrown like Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors, never inhabited (weight 6.0); The fate of Lot's wife (weight 5.8); The men of Sodom are exceedingly wicked (weight 5.2); God rains sulfur and fire from heaven on cities (weight 4.8). Pair score 27.8.

Only in Lot, his guests, his daughters and the stones of sijjil: The angels tell Lot the destruction is appointed for the morning: 'is not the morning near?'; Lot wishes he had strength or a strong support to take refuge in; The angels tell Lot who sent them and what they will do [divergence between the texts]; Only Lot's household is brought out of the doomed city; What Lot says to the townsmen; How Lot receives the heavenly guests [divergence between the texts]; When Lot leaves the city and when the destruction falls [divergence between the texts]; Lot's townspeople turn on him; What falls from heaven on Sodom; Command not to look back while fleeing a doomed place; Lot's wife is among those who stay behind and perish; Stones of baked clay (sijjil), in layers, each marked by the Lord, rain on the town; and 3 more.

Only in Lot and the destruction of his town: The host is troubled and helpless on account of the angelic guests, fearing for them; Lot's people approach men, cut off the road (highway robbery) and commit abominations in their assembly (nadi); Abraham's plea when told that the city of Lot will be destroyed [divergence between the texts]; How Lot receives the divine messengers [divergence between the texts]; God's messengers announce that they are sent to destroy the city; The sin of Sodom was pride, surfeit of bread and careless ease, not strengthening the hand of the poor and needy; Hero bargains with God to spare a city for the sake of a few righteous (50 down to 10); God appears as three men who visit the patriarch; Wife who looks back is turned into a pillar of salt; Deniers dare the prophet: 'Bring us what you threaten, if you are truthful'.

title: Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi ↔ Noah called a madman; the ark and the boiling oven
summary: 7 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A specific sign marks the moment to board (weight 6.3); The flood waters are hot or boiling (weight 6.0); A member of the hero's family is lost (weight 5.8); Animals taken aboard in pairs (weight 5.8); Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood (weight 5.2); Hero builds a vessel on divine instruction (weight 5.2); Hero's family saved with him (weight 4.5). Pair score 38.7.

Only in Noah, the boiling oven, the lost son and al-Judi: Embark: 'in the name of God be its sailing and its mooring'; God commands: 'Earth, swallow your water; sky, withhold!' and the water subsides; Noah reminds God that his son is of his family and God's promise is true; The elite scorn the prophet because only the lowest of them follow him; God answers that the drowned son is not of Noah's family: 'he is a deed not righteous'; The prophet's stories are 'tidings of the unseen' unknown to him and his people before; The ark sails through waves like mountains; What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest; What God says of later generations after the flood: no repeat, or punishment to come [contrast between the texts]; How the flood waters are stopped and subside [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's opponents object that only the lowliest follow him; he refuses to drive the believers away; Someone seeks refuge on a mountain and is drowned; and 22 more.

Only in Noah called a madman; the ark and the boiling oven: God forbids the prophet to address him on behalf of those who did wrong: they will be drowned; The flood hero prays to be landed at a blessed landing place; What the flood hero does when the vessel comes to rest [divergence between the texts]; When and from where the flood waters come [divergence between the texts]; The prophet's people object that he is only a human like them; had God willed he would have sent angels; Whether the flood hero speaks to his people before the flood [divergence between the texts]; Why God destroyed a generation or a people [divergence between the texts]; Who is saved with the hero from the destruction, and why [divergence between the texts]; Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents; Officers call the visiting prophet 'this madman' (meshugga').

title: Salih, the she-camel and the Shout ↔ Shu'ayb - measures, the prayer that commands, the clan
summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: A people is destroyed by the Shout / Blast (al-sayha) (weight 6.7); Refrain 'away with...' (bu'dan li-) the destroyed people (weight 6.0); The destroyed are as if they had never lived in their land (weight 5.8); Morning finds the destroyed lying prostrate (jathimin) in their dwellings (weight 5.6); Prophet's refrain to his people: 'Worship God; you have no god other than him' (weight 5.2). Pair score 29.2.

Only in Salih, the she-camel and the Shout: The people tell their prophet he had been their hope before this; After the crime the people are given three days' enjoyment in their homes before destruction; The people hamstring (slaughter) God's she-camel and so seal their doom; A she-camel of God is given as a sign; she must be left to graze unharmed; Unbelievers defend their practice as what they found their fathers doing; First human shaped from dust, clay or soil.

Only in Shu'ayb - measures, the prayer that commands, the clan: The people mock: 'Does your prayer command you that we abandon our fathers' gods or our way with our wealth?'; The prophet does not wish to do himself what he forbids them; he wants only reform; What God leaves you (baqiyyat Allah) is better than dishonest gain; Only the prophet's clan keeps the people from stoning him; Prophet tells deniers 'Wait, I too am waiting'; Roll call of destroyed peoples: Noah's, Ad, Thamud, Abraham's people, Midian and the overturned cities; Honest balances, weights, ephah and hin are commanded.

title: Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50) ↔ Iblis's threat to bridle Adam's offspring; sea peril; the honored children of Adam (Surah 17:61-72)
summary: 6 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity (weight 6.3); Satan has no authority over God's sincere servants, only over those who follow him (weight 6.3); The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man (weight 5.8); The devil asks for and is granted respite until the day the dead are raised (weight 5.8); God commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do (weight 5.8); First human shaped from dust, clay or soil (weight 4.6). Pair score 34.4.

Only in Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50): The pious are in gardens and springs, entering in peace and security; Hell has seven gates, each with an assigned portion of the damned; The jinn were created before humans from smokeless or scorching fire; In paradise no fatigue touches them and they are never expelled from it; God removes all rancor from the hearts of those in paradise; Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils [divergence between the texts]; God expels Iblis as accursed (rajim) with a curse until the Day of Judgment; Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils.

Only in Iblis's threat to bridle Adam's offspring; sea peril; the honored children of Adam (Surah 17:61-72): Whoever is blind in this world will be blind in the hereafter and further astray; On judgment day every people is called with its leader (imam); God lets Iblis incite humans with his voice, his cavalry and infantry, sharing their wealth and children; Threat: God could send a storm of stones on land or a shattering wind at sea; Whoever is given his book in his right hand has an easy reckoning; whoever is given it behind his back cries for destruction; In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued; In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued [contrast between the texts]; In distress, at sea or otherwise, people call on God alone, then return to polytheism once rescued [divergence between the texts]; God honored the children of Adam, carried them on land and sea and preferred them above much of creation; The devil argues he is better than man because he was made of fire and man of clay; The earth opens its mouth and swallows rebels alive into Sheol.

title: Exodus, the calf and the wilderness ↔ Twelve tribes, twelve springs, and the word changed at the gate
summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Twelve springs in the wilderness [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Israel told to enter the town's gate prostrating and say 'hitta' (remission); the wrongdoers change the word (weight 6.3); Prophet strikes a rock and water flows out for the people (weight 6.3); Oasis with twelve springs and seventy palm trees (weight 6.0); God leads the people in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night (weight 5.1). Pair score 29.9.

Only in Exodus, the calf and the wilderness: Israelites who demanded to see God are struck by a thunderbolt and then raised after their death; Who or what parts the sea [divergence between the texts]; Israel's belief or disbelief in Moses after the sea [divergence between the texts]; The cloud over Israel in the wilderness: guide or shade [divergence between the texts]; Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt; Longing for fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions and garlic of Egypt [divergence between the texts]; God's pardon after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain [divergence between the texts]; The killing of Israelites after the golden calf [divergence between the texts]; Wind brings quail in vast quantity to feed the people [divergence between the texts]; Humans seeing God [contrast between the texts]; People propose appointing a leader to go back to Egypt; and 13 more.

Only in Twelve tribes, twelve springs, and the word changed at the gate: Twelve springs gush from the struck rock, one drinking place for each tribe; Among Moses' people is a community that guides by the truth and acts justly by it; Prophet strikes a rock and water flows out for the people [divergence between the texts]; Manna and quail are followed by a punishment from God [divergence between the texts]; The wrongdoers replace the word they were told with another, and a plague falls from heaven; Twelve sons of the patriarch listed by their mothers; Quail come up in the evening and cover the camp.

sides.note: Twelve springs: fa-nbajasat minhu thnatā ʿashrata ʿaynan qad ʿalima kullu unāsin mashrabahum vs šᵉtêm ʿeśrēh ʿênōt mayim wᵉšibʿîm tᵉmārîm (ʿayn = ʿayin). Elim's natural oasis becomes the miracle of the struck rock, and the twelve springs are tied to the twelve tribes (ithnatay ʿashrata asbāṭan; asbāṭ = šᵉbāṭîm); the seventy palms are dropped.

Only in Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh; the contest with the magicians: The contest with the magicians is set for a festival day (yawm al-zīna) at forenoon with the people assembled; From the earth humans were created, into it they return, and from it they are brought forth again; Formula: 'Peace be on whoever follows the guidance'; Pharaoh asks about the fate of former generations; the answer: their knowledge is with God in a book; The prophets are told to speak to the tyrant with gentle words, that he may take heed or fear; The defeated magicians fall prostrate and declare faith in the Lord of Moses and Aaron [divergence between the texts]; King defies the prophet: 'Who is YHWH that I should obey him?' passages.text: قَالَ ءَامَنتُمْ لَهُۥ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ إِنَّهُۥ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَكُمُ ٱلسِّحْرَ فَلَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُم مِّنْ خِلَٰفٍ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ

sides.note: Pharaoh's response to the sign: Exod 7:13 wa-yyeḥĕzaq lēv Parʿōh wə-lōʾ šāmaʿ ʾălēhem ka-ʾăšer dibber YHWH, the heart hardened as God foretold (God hardens it himself at 14:4, 14:8); Q 26:49 has no hardening and no divine agency, only Pharaoh's rage: āmantum lahu qabla an ādhana lakum innahu la-kabīrukumu lladhī ʿallamakumu s-siḥra, with a threat of amputation and crucifixion.

passages.text: وَجَحَدُوا۟ بِهَا وَٱسْتَيْقَنَتْهَآ أَنفُسُهُمْ ظُلْمًا وَعُلُوًّا فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ

sides.note: Why Egypt refuses: Exod 8:15 the magicians admit ʾeṣbaʿ ʾĕlōhîm hîʾ, yet wa-yyeḥĕzaq lēv Parʿōh ... ka-ʾăšer dibber YHWH, the heart is hardened as God foretold; Q 27:14 wa-jaḥadū bihā wa-staiqanathā anfusuhum ẓulman wa-ʿuluwwan, they rejected the signs though inwardly convinced, out of wrongdoing and arrogance. Refusal by God's design becomes knowing, self-chosen denial.

passages.text: وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُۥ فَإِذَا هِىَ بَيْضَآءُ لِلنَّٰظِرِينَ

sides.note: wa-nazaʿa yadahu fa-idhā hiya bayḍāʾu li-n-nāẓirīna ~ wə-hinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg: the white hand. In Exodus it is leprous (məṣōraʿat), shown to Moses at the bush and meant for the Israelites (4:8-9, 4:30); in the Quran it is simply 'white for the beholders', shown to Pharaoh and his court, with no disease.

passages.text: وَأَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فِى جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضَآءَ مِنْ غَيْرِ سُوٓءٍ فِى تِسْعِ ءَايَٰتٍ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَقَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ

sides.note: wa-adkhil yadaka fī jaybika takhruj bayḍāʾa min ghayri sūʾin ~ hāvēʾ nāʾ yādəkā bə-ḥêqekā ... wə-hinnēh yādô məṣōraʿat ka-ššāleg: hand into the bosom (jayb / ḥêq) and out white. The Quran's 'without evil' (min ghayri sūʾ) excludes exactly what Exodus says, that the hand was leprous (məṣōraʿat), and needs no second step of restoring it (4:7).

passages.text: وَلَهُمْ عَلَىَّ ذَنۢبٌ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ
قَالَ كَلَّا فَٱذْهَبَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّا مَعَكُم مُّسْتَمِعُونَ

sides.note: Fear of being killed for the old killing: in Exodus God removes it by fact, kî mētû kol hā-ʾănāšîm ham-məvaqšîm ʾet nafšekā; in the Quran Moses raises it himself (wa-lahum ʿalayya dhanbun fa-akhāfu an yaqtulūni), and God answers with his presence, 'kallā ... innā maʿakum mustamiʿūn'.

passages.text: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّى قَتَلْتُ مِنْهُمْ نَفْسًا فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ

sides.note: rabbi innī qataltu minhum nafsan fa-akhāfu an yaqtulūni ~ kî mētû kol hā-ʾănāšîm ham-məvaqšîm ʾet nafšekā: the old killing as an obstacle to going back. In Exodus God removes it unasked, in the Quran Moses raises it at the call.

matches.label: Aaron's role beside Moses and how he is appointed

passages.text: وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِى وَلَا يَنطَلِقُ لِسَانِى فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَٰرُونَ
قَالَ كَلَّا فَٱذْهَبَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ إِنَّا مَعَكُم مُّسْتَمِعُونَ

sides.note: God's answer to Moses' reluctance: wa-yyiḥar ʾap YHWH bə-Mōše ... hălōʾ ʾAhărōn ʾāḥîkā ... wə-ʾattâ tihyeh lô lēʾlōhîm (anger; Aaron as mouth, Moses as God to him) ~ qāla kallā fa-dhhabā bi-āyātinā innā maʿakum mustamiʿūna: no anger and no 'as God'; both are sent as equals (fa-dhhabā, dual).

passages.text: وَأَخِى هَٰرُونُ هُوَ أَفْصَحُ مِنِّى لِسَانًا فَأَرْسِلْهُ مَعِىَ رِدْءًا يُصَدِّقُنِىٓ إِنِّىٓ أَخَافُ أَن يُكَذِّبُونِ
قَالَ سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ وَنَجْعَلُ لَكُمَا سُلْطَٰنًا فَلَا يَصِلُونَ إِلَيْكُمَا بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أَنتُمَا وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكُمَا ٱلْغَٰلِبُونَ

sides.note: Aaron's eloquence: in Exodus Moses says he is heavy of mouth, and God, angry, proposes Aaron himself: wa-yyiḥar ʾap YHWH bə-Mōše ... yādaʿtî kî dabbēr yədabbēr hûʾ ... wə-śamtā ʾet had-dəvārîm bə-fîw. In the Quran Moses proposes him, wa-akhī Hārūnu huwa afṣaḥu minnī lisānan fa-arsilhu maʿiya ridʾan yuṣaddiqunī, and God agrees without anger: sa-nashuddu ʿaḍudaka bi-akhīka. Aaron is a supporting witness (ridʾ, yuṣaddiqunī), not a mouth for Moses as God.

Only in The Garden: offspring joined with parents, the cup without idle talk, youths like pearls; the run of 'or...?' challenges: The blessed question each other and recall that they used to be fearful among their families, and God saved them from the scorching wind (samum); In paradise they pass a cup to one another in which is no idle talk (laghw) or sin; If they saw a fragment of the sky falling they would say 'heaped-up clouds'; Glorify God when you rise, in the night, and at the retreat of the stars (dawn); Do they have a ladder (sullam) by which they eavesdrop on heaven? title: The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall ↔ Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50)
summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: The expelled devil vows to lie in wait on the straight path and mislead humanity (weight 6.3); The devil (Iblis) alone refuses to bow to the first man (weight 5.8); The devil asks for and is granted respite until the day the dead are raised (weight 5.8); God commands the angels to prostrate before the first man, and they do (weight 5.8); First human shaped from dust, clay or soil (weight 4.6). Pair score 28.2.

Only in The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall: Man and wife are addressed, tempted and eat together; the woman is not singled out; The first humans are sent down to earth to live and enjoy provision for a time; The devil will come at humans from before, behind, right and left; The first couple confess 'we have wronged ourselves' and ask God's forgiveness; On the earth humans live, in it they die, and from it they will be brought out; The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals; The tempter swears an oath to the first couple that he is their sincere adviser; God vows to fill hell with the devil and all who follow him; Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans; God casts the proud being out from the mountain of God and destroys him from among the stones of fire, hurling him to earth before kings; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; God gives the adversary (Satan) leave to act against humans; and 17 more.

Only in Man from black mud, jinn from scorching fire, and Iblis's refusal (Surah 15:26-50): The pious are in gardens and springs, entering in peace and security; Hell has seven gates, each with an assigned portion of the damned; The jinn were created before humans from smokeless or scorching fire; In paradise no fatigue touches them and they are never expelled from it; God removes all rancor from the hearts of those in paradise; Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils [divergence between the texts]; Satan has no authority over God's sincere servants, only over those who follow him; God expels Iblis as accursed (rajim) with a curse until the Day of Judgment; Deity breathes the breath of life into the first human's nostrils.

title: The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall ↔ Adam's forgetting, Iblis, the tree of immortality and the descent
summary: 9 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: Satan whispers (waswasa) to tempt humans (weight 6.7); Enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed: head bruised, heel struck [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit [divergence between the texts] (weight 6.3); Enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed: head bruised, heel struck (weight 6.3); Fig leaves sewn into coverings (weight 6.3); Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked (weight 6.3); First humans expelled from the garden (weight 6.0); A cunning serpent persuades the woman to eat the forbidden fruit (weight 6.0); God plants a garden (Eden) in the east and places the first human there (weight 5.6). Pair score 55.7.

Only in The prostration to Adam, Iblis' refusal and the fall: Man and wife are addressed, tempted and eat together; the woman is not singled out; The first humans are sent down to earth to live and enjoy provision for a time; The devil will come at humans from before, behind, right and left; The first couple confess 'we have wronged ourselves' and ask God's forgiveness; On the earth humans live, in it they die, and from it they will be brought out; The tempter claims the tree is forbidden only lest the couple become angels or immortals; The tempter swears an oath to the first couple that he is their sincere adviser; God vows to fill hell with the devil and all who follow him; God casts the proud being out from the mountain of God and destroys him from among the stones of fire, hurling him to earth before kings; How the first couple answer God after eating: shifting the blame or confessing [divergence between the texts]; God gives the adversary (Satan) leave to act against humans; Sinner hides from God, who calls 'Where are you?' [divergence between the texts]; and 13 more.

Only in Adam's forgetting, Iblis, the tree of immortality and the descent: God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve; In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat; Whoever turned from God's reminder is raised blind on judgment day: as he forgot the signs, so he is forgotten; The tempter offers 'the tree of immortality and a kingdom that never decays'; God made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot and lacked resolve [divergence between the texts]; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness; Adam receives words from his Lord and God turns to him in forgiveness [divergence between the texts]; God commands the angels to prostrate to Adam; all do except Iblis, who refuses; Eating opens their eyes and they know they are naked [divergence between the texts]; In the garden Adam will not hunger, be naked, thirst or suffer the sun's heat [divergence between the texts]; The tempter offers 'the tree of immortality and a kingdom that never decays' [divergence between the texts]; A tree whose fruit gives eternal life.

sides.note: Gen: wə-ʾêvāh ʾāšît bênkhā û-vên hā-ʾiššāh û-vên zarʿăkhā û-vên zarʿāh, enmity set by God between serpent and woman and their seed. Q: qāla hbiṭū baʿḍukum li-baʿḍin ʿaduwwun, plural, a mutual enmity of those sent down (humans and Satan, 7:22 inna l-shayṭāna lakumā ʿaduww). Gen's enmity is between serpent and woman and their seed, and the way back is barred by cherubim. Q's enmity is among those sent down, and Q adds a promise of guidance, fa-immā yaʾtiyannakum minnī hudan fa-mani ttabaʿa hudāya fa-lā yaḍillu wa-lā yashqā.

title: Six days, the Throne, winds and rain as proof of resurrection ↔ The moving shadow, the night garment, the two seas and the constellations
summary: 5 shared motifs, found by the separate reads; not yet compared side by side.

evidence.text: Shared motifs, rarest first: God sends the winds as heralds before his mercy and sends down pure water from the sky (weight 5.4); After creating the heavens and earth God established himself on the Throne (istawa 'ala l-'arsh) (weight 5.2); Creation is completed in six days (weight 5.2); Sun and moon are set to rule day and night and mark signs and seasons (weight 4.7); Rain from the sky gives life to the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection (weight 4.4). sides.note: Who throws the staff, and how. sides.note: Exod: Aaron's staff (wayyašlēk ʾahărōn ʾet-maṭṭēhû ... wayhî lətannîn), and the magicians really do the same, wayyaʿăśû gam-hēm ḥarṭummê miṣrayim bəlahăṭêhem kēn ... wayyihyû lətannînim, before wayyiblaʿ maṭṭēh-ʾahărōn ʾet-maṭṭōtām. passages.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֡שׁ לְכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁר עָמְד֨וּ עָלָ֜יו הַאַתֶּ֣ם תְּרִיב֣וּן לַבַּ֗עַל אִם אַתֶּם֙ תּוֹשִׁיע֣וּן אוֹת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָרִ֥יב ל֛וֹ יוּמַ֖ת עַד הַבֹּ֑קֶר אִם אֱלֹהִ֥ים הוּא֙ יָ֣רֶב ל֔וֹ כִּ֥י נָתַ֖ץ אֶֽת מִזְבְּחֽוֹ
וַיִּקְרָא ל֥וֹ בַיּוֹם הַה֖וּא יְרֻבַּ֣עַל לֵאמֹ֑ר יָ֤רֶב בּוֹ֙ הַבַּ֔עַל כִּ֥י נָתַ֖ץ אֶֽת מִזְבְּחֽוֹ

sides.note: The same argument from the idol's helplessness: ʾim-ʾĕlōhîm hûʾ yāreb lô kî nātaṣ ʾet-mizbəḥô, 'if he is a god let him contend for himself'; bal faʿalahu kabīruhum hādhā fa-sʾalūhum in kānū yanṭiqūn, 'ask them, if they can speak'. In Judg the idolatrous father Joash says it to protect his son; in Q Abraham says it to shame the people, and they are turned on their heads (nukisū ʿalā ruʾūsihim).

passages.text: (6:25) וַיְהִי֮ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַהוּא֒ וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ יְהוָ֗ה קַ֤ח אֶת פַּר הַשּׁוֹר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וּפַ֥ר הַשֵּׁנִ֖י שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים וְהָרַסְתָּ֗ אֶת מִזְבַּ֤ח הַבַּ֨עַל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וְאֶת הָאֲשֵׁרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר עָלָ֖יו תִּכְרֹֽת (6:26) וּבָנִ֨יתָ מִזְבֵּ֜חַ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ עַ֣ל רֹ֧אשׁ הַמָּע֛וֹז הַזֶּ֖ה בַּמַּֽעֲרָכָ֑ה וְלָֽקַחְתָּ֙ אֶת הַפָּ֣ר הַשֵּׁנִ֔י וְהַעֲלִ֣יתָ עוֹלָ֔ה בַּעֲצֵ֥י הָאֲשֵׁרָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּכְרֹֽת (6:27) וַיִּקַּ֨ח גִּדְע֜וֹן עֲשָׂרָ֤ה אֲנָשִׁים֙ מֵֽעֲבָדָ֔יו וַיַּ֕עַשׂ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלָ֖יו יְהוָ֑ה וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יָרֵא֩ אֶת בֵּ֨ית אָבִ֜יו וְאֶת אַנְשֵׁ֥י הָעִ֛יר מֵעֲשׂ֥וֹת יוֹמָ֖ם וַיַּ֥עַשׂ לָֽיְלָה (6:28) וַיַּשְׁכִּ֜ימוּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י הָעִיר֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּ֤ה נֻתַּץ֙ מִזְבַּ֣ח הַבַּ֔עַל וְהָאֲשֵׁרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר עָלָ֖יו כֹּרָ֑תָה וְאֵת֙ הַפָּ֣ר הַשֵּׁנִ֔י הֹֽעֲלָ֔ה עַל הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ הַבָּנֽוּי

וַיְהִי֮ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַהוּא֒ וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ יְהוָ֗ה קַ֤ח אֶת פַּר הַשּׁוֹר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וּפַ֥ר הַשֵּׁנִ֖י שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים וְהָרַסְתָּ֗ אֶת מִזְבַּ֤ח הַבַּ֨עַל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יךָ וְאֶת הָאֲשֵׁרָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר עָלָ֖יו תִּכְרֹֽת

וַיִּקַּ֨ח גִּדְע֜וֹן עֲשָׂרָ֤ה אֲנָשִׁים֙ מֵֽעֲבָדָ֔יו וַיַּ֕עַשׂ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלָ֖יו יְהוָ֑ה וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יָרֵא֩ אֶת בֵּ֨ית אָבִ֜יו וְאֶת אַנְשֵׁ֥י הָעִ֛יר מֵעֲשׂ֥וֹת יוֹמָ֖ם וַיַּ֥עַשׂ לָֽיְלָה

Only in Noah in the Quran: Someone seeks refuge on a mountain and is drowned; Vessel described by its planks and fastenings; A specific sign marks the moment to board; Hero blessed on leaving the vessel; The flood waters are hot or boiling; Hero's life or mission spans 950 years; People mock the hero while he builds the vessel; A member of the hero's family is lost; Hero asks the deity to judge or destroy his opponents; Hero warns or preaches to his people before the flood; Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger.

Only in The Flood (full read): Clean animals taken aboard by sevens, unclean by pairs; Flood events given exact calendar dates (year of hero's life, month, day); Rain or flood lasts forty days and forty nights; God regrets having made humankind and is grieved in his heart; God himself shuts the vessel's door behind the hero; A dove returns with an olive leaf in its beak; A raven is sent out and does not return (goes to and fro); Seven days pass between the warning or boarding and the onset of the flood; Vessel has several decks, a side door and a roof opening or window; God sends a wind (ruah) over the earth to make the waters subside; Angels object that the new human will corrupt the earth and shed blood while they praise God; When the water overflowed God carried 'you' in the running ship (al-jariya) as a reminder for retaining ears [divergence between the texts]; and 37 more.

summary: يَهْبِطُ (yahbiṭu, “down”) occurs in 8 verses; 5 of them (62%) are in the Adam and Iblis narrative, which is 1% of the Quran, across 3 surahs. The more common same-gloss word أَنزَلَ (ʾanzala, 162 verses) has only 0% of its verses there.

passages.text: فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ
قُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِنْهَا جَمِيعًا فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ

وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نَّصْبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامٍ وَٰحِدٍ فَٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخْرِجْ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنۢبِتُ ٱلْأَرْضُ مِنۢ بَقْلِهَا وَقِثَّآئِهَا وَفُومِهَا وَعَدَسِهَا وَبَصَلِهَا قَالَ أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِى هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِى هُوَ خَيْرٌ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِصْرًا فَإِنَّ لَكُم مَّا سَأَلْتُمْ وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلذِّلَّةُ وَٱلْمَسْكَنَةُ وَبَآءُو بِغَضَبٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ يَكْفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ ٱلنَّبِيِّۦنَ بِغَيْرِ ٱلْحَقِّ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَوا۟ وَّكَانُوا۟ يَعْتَدُونَ

ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِىَ كَٱلْحِجَارَةِ أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً وَإِنَّ مِنَ ٱلْحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنْهُ ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ فَيَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ ٱلْمَآءُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَهْبِطُ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ
قَالَ فَٱهْبِطْ مِنْهَا فَمَا يَكُونُ لَكَ أَن تَتَكَبَّرَ فِيهَا فَٱخْرُجْ إِنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰغِرِينَ
قَالَ ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ
قِيلَ يَٰنُوحُ ٱهْبِطْ بِسَلَٰمٍ مِّنَّا وَبَرَكَٰتٍ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰٓ أُمَمٍ مِّمَّن مَّعَكَ وَأُمَمٌ سَنُمَتِّعُهُمْ ثُمَّ يَمَسُّهُم مِّنَّا عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
قَالَ ٱهْبِطَا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًۢا بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ

passages.text: وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ ءَازَرَ أَتَتَّخِذُ أَصْنَامًا ءَالِهَةً إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰكَ وَقَوْمَكَ فِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ

وَجَٰوَزْنَا بِبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلْبَحْرَ فَأَتَوْا۟ عَلَىٰ قَوْمٍ يَعْكُفُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَصْنَامٍ لَّهُمْ قَالُوا۟ يَٰمُوسَى ٱجْعَل لَّنَآ إِلَٰهًا كَمَا لَهُمْ ءَالِهَةٌ قَالَ إِنَّكُمْ قَوْمٌ تَجْهَلُونَ
وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِيمُ رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْ هَٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدَ ءَامِنًا وَٱجْنُبْنِى وَبَنِىَّ أَن نَّعْبُدَ ٱلْأَصْنَامَ
وَتَٱللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصْنَٰمَكُم بَعْدَ أَن تُوَلُّوا۟ مُدْبِرِينَ
قَالُوا۟ نَعْبُدُ أَصْنَامًا فَنَظَلُّ لَهَا عَٰكِفِينَ

passages.text: وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِۦٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تَذْبَحُوا۟ بَقَرَةً قَالُوٓا۟ أَتَتَّخِذُنَا هُزُوًا قَالَ أَعُوذُ بِٱللَّهِ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْجَٰهِلِينَ
قَالُوا۟ ٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِىَ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَّا فَارِضٌ وَلَا بِكْرٌ عَوَانٌۢ بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ فَٱفْعَلُوا۟ مَا تُؤْمَرُونَ
قَالُوا۟ ٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا لَوْنُهَا قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ صَفْرَآءُ فَاقِعٌ لَّوْنُهَا تَسُرُّ ٱلنَّٰظِرِينَ

قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَّا ذَلُولٌ تُثِيرُ ٱلْأَرْضَ وَلَا تَسْقِى ٱلْحَرْثَ مُسَلَّمَةٌ لَّا شِيَةَ فِيهَا قَالُوا۟ ٱلْـَٰٔنَ جِئْتَ بِٱلْحَقِّ فَذَبَحُوهَا وَمَا كَادُوا۟ يَفْعَلُونَ

وَقَالَ ٱلْمَلِكُ إِنِّىٓ أَرَىٰ سَبْعَ بَقَرَٰتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعَ سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٍ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَأُ أَفْتُونِى فِى رُءْيَٰىَ إِن كُنتُمْ لِلرُّءْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ

يُوسُفُ أَيُّهَا ٱلصِّدِّيقُ أَفْتِنَا فِى سَبْعِ بَقَرَٰتٍ سِمَانٍ يَأْكُلُهُنَّ سَبْعٌ عِجَافٌ وَسَبْعِ سُنۢبُلَٰتٍ خُضْرٍ وَأُخَرَ يَابِسَٰتٍ لَّعَلِّىٓ أَرْجِعُ إِلَى ٱلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ

إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ عَلَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَجَعَلَ أَهْلَهَا شِيَعًا يَسْتَضْعِفُ طَآئِفَةً مِّنْهُمْ يُذَبِّحُ أَبْنَآءَهُمْ وَيَسْتَحْىِۦ نِسَآءَهُمْ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ

يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَدْخُلُوا۟ بُيُوتَ ٱلنَّبِىِّ إِلَّآ أَن يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ إِلَىٰ طَعَامٍ غَيْرَ نَٰظِرِينَ إِنَىٰهُ وَلَٰكِنْ إِذَا دُعِيتُمْ فَٱدْخُلُوا۟ فَإِذَا طَعِمْتُمْ فَٱنتَشِرُوا۟ وَلَا مُسْتَـْٔنِسِينَ لِحَدِيثٍ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكُمْ كَانَ يُؤْذِى ٱلنَّبِىَّ فَيَسْتَحْىِۦ مِنكُمْ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَسْتَحْىِۦ مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ وَإِذَا سَأَلْتُمُوهُنَّ مَتَٰعًا فَسْـَٔلُوهُنَّ مِن وَرَآءِ حِجَابٍ ذَٰلِكُمْ أَطْهَرُ لِقُلُوبِكُمْ وَقُلُوبِهِنَّ وَمَا كَانَ لَكُمْ أَن تُؤْذُوا۟ رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَآ أَن تَنكِحُوٓا۟ أَزْوَٰجَهُۥ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦٓ أَبَدًا إِنَّ ذَٰلِكُمْ كَانَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ عَظِيمًا
فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُم بِٱلْحَقِّ مِنْ عِندِنَا قَالُوا۟ ٱقْتُلُوٓا۟ أَبْنَآءَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مَعَهُۥ وَٱسْتَحْيُوا۟ نِسَآءَهُمْ وَمَا كَيْدُ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ

title: Who are the Quran's Sabians?
summary: The Quran names the Sabians (al-Ṣābiʾūn) beside Jews and Christians. Candidates include the Mandaeans, the pagans of Harran, and Elchasaite baptists.

passages.text: (2:62) إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ وَٱلصَّٰبِـِٔينَ مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًا فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (5:69) إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلصَّٰبِـُٔونَ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًا فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (22:17) إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ وَٱلصَّٰبِـِٔينَ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ وَٱلْمَجُوسَ وَٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوٓا۟ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ شَهِيدٌ

title: Sargon and Moses: the infant in the sealed basket
summary: The Neo-Assyrian Sargon Birth Legend has a baby placed in a reed basket sealed with bitumen, set on the river, and raised by a water-drawer. Exodus 2 and the Quran's Moses (into al-yamm) share the motif.

passages.note: papyrus basket daubed with bitumen and pitch
passages.text: (2:1) וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אִ֖ישׁ מִבֵּ֣ית לֵוִ֑י וַיִּקַּ֖ח אֶת בַּת לֵוִֽי (2:2) וַתַּ֥הַר הָאִשָּׁ֖ה וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֹתוֹ֙ כִּי ט֣וֹב ה֔וּא וַֽתִּצְפְּנֵ֖הוּ שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה יְרָחִֽים (2:3) וְלֹא יָכְלָ֣ה עוֹד֮ הַצְּפִינוֹ֒ וַתִּֽקַּֽח לוֹ֙ תֵּ֣בַת גֹּ֔מֶא וַתַּחְמְרָ֥ה בַחֵמָ֖ר וּבַזָּ֑פֶת וַתָּ֤שֶׂם בָּהּ֙ אֶת הַיֶּ֔לֶד וַתָּ֥שֶׂם בַּסּ֖וּף עַל שְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר (2:4) וַתֵּתַצַּ֥ב אֲחֹת֖וֹ מֵרָחֹ֑ק לְדֵעָ֕ה מַה יֵּעָשֶׂ֖ה לֽוֹ (2:5) וַתֵּ֤רֶד בַּת פַּרְעֹה֙ לִרְחֹ֣ץ עַל הַיְאֹ֔ר וְנַעֲרֹתֶ֥יהָ הֹלְכֹ֖ת עַל יַ֣ד הַיְאֹ֑ר וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֶת הַתֵּבָה֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַסּ֔וּף וַתִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֶת אֲמָתָ֖הּ וַתִּקָּחֶֽהָ (2:6) וַתִּפְתַּח֙ וַתִּרְאֵ֣הוּ אֶת הַיֶּ֔לֶד וְהִנֵּה נַ֖עַר בֹּכֶ֑ה וַתַּחְמֹ֣ל עָלָ֔יו וַתֹּ֕אמֶר מִיַּלְדֵ֥י הָֽעִבְרִ֖ים זֶֽה (2:7) וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֲחֹתוֹ֮ אֶל בַּת פַּרְעֹה֒ הַאֵלֵ֗ךְ וְקָרָ֤אתִי לָךְ֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה מֵינֶ֔קֶת מִ֖ן הָעִבְרִיֹּ֑ת וְתֵינִ֥ק לָ֖ךְ אֶת הַיָּֽלֶד (2:8) וַתֹּֽאמֶר לָ֥הּ בַּת פַּרְעֹ֖ה לֵ֑כִי וַתֵּ֨לֶךְ֙ הָֽעַלְמָ֔ה וַתִּקְרָ֖א אֶת אֵ֥ם הַיָּֽלֶד (2:9) וַתֹּ֧אמֶר לָ֣הּ בַּת פַּרְעֹ֗ה הֵילִ֜יכִי אֶת הַיֶּ֤לֶד הַזֶּה֙ וְהֵינִקִ֣הוּ לִ֔י וַאֲנִ֖י אֶתֵּ֣ן אֶת שְׂכָרֵ֑ךְ וַתִּקַּ֧ח הָאִשָּׁ֛ה הַיֶּ֖לֶד וַתְּנִיקֵֽהוּ (2:10) וַיִגְדַּ֣ל הַיֶּ֗לֶד וַתְּבִאֵ֨הוּ֙ לְבַת פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַֽיְהִי לָ֖הּ לְבֵ֑ן וַתִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַתֹּ֕אמֶר כִּ֥י מִן הַמַּ֖יִם מְשִׁיתִֽהוּ

passages.text: (20:38) إِذْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ مَا يُوحَىٰٓ (20:39) أَنِ ٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلتَّابُوتِ فَٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ فَلْيُلْقِهِ ٱلْيَمُّ بِٱلسَّاحِلِ يَأْخُذْهُ عَدُوٌّ لِّى وَعَدُوٌّ لَّهُۥ وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِّنِّى وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَىٰ عَيْنِىٓ (28:7) وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ فَإِذَا خِفْتِ عَلَيْهِ فَأَلْقِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ وَلَا تَخَافِى وَلَا تَحْزَنِىٓ إِنَّا رَآدُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ وَجَاعِلُوهُ مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ (28:8) فَٱلْتَقَطَهُۥٓ ءَالُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَنًا إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا كَانُوا۟ خَٰطِـِٔينَ (28:9) وَقَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ فِرْعَوْنَ قُرَّتُ عَيْنٍ لِّى وَلَكَ لَا تَقْتُلُوهُ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَنفَعَنَآ أَوْ نَتَّخِذَهُۥ وَلَدًا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ (28:10) وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤَادُ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ فَٰرِغًا إِن كَادَتْ لَتُبْدِى بِهِۦ لَوْلَآ أَن رَّبَطْنَا عَلَىٰ قَلْبِهَا لِتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ (28:11) وَقَالَتْ لِأُخْتِهِۦ قُصِّيهِ فَبَصُرَتْ بِهِۦ عَن جُنُبٍ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ (28:12) وَحَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلْمَرَاضِعَ مِن قَبْلُ فَقَالَتْ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَهْلِ بَيْتٍ يَكْفُلُونَهُۥ لَكُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُۥ نَٰصِحُونَ (28:13) فَرَدَدْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّهِۦ كَىْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ وَلِتَعْلَمَ أَنَّ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ

title: Whoever saves one life
summary: Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 teaches that destroying one life is like destroying a world, and saving one is like saving a world. Quran 5:32 states the same principle as decreed for the Children of Israel.

passages.text: مِنْ أَجْلِ ذَٰلِكَ كَتَبْنَا عَلَىٰ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ أَنَّهُۥ مَن قَتَلَ نَفْسًۢا بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسَادٍ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعًا وَمَنْ أَحْيَاهَا فَكَأَنَّمَآ أَحْيَا ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعًا وَلَقَدْ جَآءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُنَا بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ ثُمَّ إِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِّنْهُم بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ لَمُسْرِفُونَ

evidence.text: The Quran explicitly frames it as a precept for the Children of Israel.

summary: Dara Shikoh translated 50 Upanishads into Persian as the Sirr-i Akbar (1657). Anquetil-Duperron's Latin version (Oupnek'hat, 1801–02) is how Schopenhauer read them.

title: Seven Sleepers and the People of the Cave
summary: Youths fleeing persecution sleep in a cave for centuries and wake to a changed world. Told in Syriac (Jacob of Serugh), Greek, and Latin sources, and in Quran 18:9–26.

title: tannūr: the oven that boiled at the Flood
summary: Akkadian tinūru (oven) reached Aramaic, Hebrew, and Arabic. In the Quran's Noah narrative the sign of the Flood is that the tannūr boiled over.

فَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْهِ أَنِ ٱصْنَعِ ٱلْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ فَٱسْلُكْ فِيهَا مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ مِنْهُمْ وَلَا تُخَٰطِبْنِى فِى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُم مُّغْرَقُونَ

title: Plotinus as the 'Theology of Aristotle'
summary: An Arabic paraphrase of Plotinus' Enneads IV–VI circulated as the 'Theology of Aristotle' (al-Kindi's circle, 9th c.) and shaped Islamic Neoplatonism.

title: Ancient treaty form and Deuteronomy's covenant
summary: Deuteronomy follows the structure of ancient Near Eastern vassal treaties: preamble, history, stipulations, deposit, witnesses, curses and blessings.

evidence.text: Mendenhall (1954) argued for the Hittite model. Many scholars now consider Neo-Assyrian treaties the closer parallel. Which source is closer is the open question.

title: al-yamm: the sea word reserved for Moses
summary: The Quran's usual word for sea is bahr, but al-yamm appears 8 times across 4 surahs, always in the Moses/Pharaoh narrative. It is the Semitic sea word shared with Hebrew yam, Ugaritic Yam, and Mandaic yama, and borrowed into New Kingdom Egyptian.

lexical.gloss: Sea, the sea god opposed to Baal

passages.text: מַרְכְּבֹ֥ת פַּרְעֹ֛ה וְחֵיל֖וֹ יָרָ֣ה בַיָּ֑ם וּמִבְחַ֥ר שָֽׁלִשָׁ֖יו טֻבְּע֥וּ בְיַם סֽוּף

evidence.text: 8 occurrences of the lemma, verified with the Quran word concordance (root ي م م); the other root hits are the unrelated verb tayammum (2:267, 4:43, 5:6).
Dispersion: 4 surahs (7, 20, 28, 51), 1 narrative. Concentrated in one story while spread across the text.
Synonym-choice skew: bahr is the general word for sea elsewhere in the Quran.
Egyptian ym is a Semitic loanword, so this is shared Semitic vocabulary fitting the Egyptian setting, not an Egyptian borrowing into Arabic.
